title: Add regression/integration tests + CI guardrails for critical RBAC v2 permissions
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Background
- As part of RBAC v2 rollout, we need strong regression protection for sensitive actions. We’ve already had one incident-class issue where a streaming route lacked/bypassed permission enforcement (see GitHub: sources/github/redwood/pr-28391-hotfix-permission-check-bypass-on-streaming-route.json).
- This ticket adds end-to-end/integration tests for “critical permissions” and introduces CI guardrails so we don’t ship new sensitive endpoints without permission annotations and test coverage.

Goals
1) Add stable integration tests that validate allow/deny behavior for critical sensitive actions across:
   - API Gateway authz middleware (deny-by-default)
   - Control Plane services (permission annotations + enforcement)
   - Audit log emission includes authz decision context (for key actions)
2) Add CI coverage gates:
   - Prevent merge if a new/changed sensitive endpoint is unannotated
   - Prevent merge if critical permission tests are missing or failing
   - Provide actionable failure output (what endpoint/permission is missing)

Non-goals
- Full fuzzing of all permissions (we’ll focus on a curated critical set).
- Building a full policy simulation environment for customers.

Critical actions in scope (initial set)
- API key + credential management
  - Rotate API keys
  - Create/revoke API keys
  - Update key restrictions/scopes (where supported)
- RBAC administration
  - Create/update/delete roles (custom roles)
  - Create/update/delete role bindings
  - Invite/deactivate users; change user role assignments
- Routing/model serving policy
  - Modify routing policy (e.g., traffic shifting / fallback policies)
  - Change model pinning / rollout policy for an environment
- Audit logging + exports
  - Export audit logs (including SIEM export path where applicable)
- Private/Dedicated admin operations (where test harness supports)
  - Bootstrap admin binding (Private installer) is tracked separately; here we validate that a non-admin cannot perform admin-only actions in the Private control plane API surface

Acceptance criteria
- Integration tests exist for each “critical action” above with the following coverage:
  - Deny when subject lacks permission (expect 403 + standardized reason code)
  - Allow when subject has permission (expect 2xx + side effect)
  - For at least 3 representative actions (key rotation, role binding change, routing policy edit), validate audit log event includes authz decision fields (decision allow/deny, action, scope, policy version) per the schema extension work.
- CI gate(s) implemented:
  - A coverage report step fails PRs if any endpoint in the critical list does not have a permission annotation OR is not included in the test manifest.
  - The failure output includes the endpoint/handler name + expected permission string.
- Tests run in <12 minutes in CI and are not flaky (target: <1% flakes over 2 weeks).

Proposed approach
A) Test harness / environment
- Use the existing integration test runner used by control-plane + gateway e2e tests (docker-compose in CI). Tests should execute requests through the gateway whenever possible to catch misconfig at the edge.
- Create two test principals:
  1) principal_admin: bound to built-in “Org Admin” role (or equivalent) at org scope
  2) principal_limited: bound to a minimal role that intentionally excludes the critical permission under test
- For each test case, set up:
  - Org + Project + Environment fixture (avoid reusing across tests if it increases flake)
  - Role bindings via RBAC v2 policy bundle version pinned for the test

B) Manifest-driven “critical permissions” suite
- Introduce a single manifest file (checked into repo) listing:
  - action permission string (e.g., redwood.org.api_keys.rotate)
  - endpoint(s) / route name(s)
  - required scope(s) (org/project/env)
  - expected denial reason code when missing (where deterministic)
- The manifest is what CI gates on; adding new critical action requires manifest update + test.

C) Coverage guardrail options (pick one; implement the simplest viable)
Option 1 (preferred): Endpoint annotation scrape + diff
- Scrape permission annotations from compiled service metadata (or static annotation registry) and compare against:
  - The manifest list (must exist)
  - A “sensitive endpoints” registry (derived from permission inventory)
- Fail CI if any listed endpoint lacks an annotation OR if an annotation exists but is not in the registry.

Option 2: Gateway route table enforcement
- Generate a gateway route table at build time and ensure each route in a “protected” group has a permission requirement.

CI gate behavior
- On PR, run:
  - unit tests (existing)
  - integration suite “authz_critical_permissions” (new)
  - script: verify-permission-coverage (new)
- Gate should be soft-launchable behind a repo flag for the first week (warn-only) to avoid blocking on existing gaps, then enforce after backlog is cleared.

Implementation notes / links
- Confluence: API standards – authorization check patterns
  - sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/authorization-check-patterns.json
- GitHub PRs (related):
  - PR-28159 gateway middleware deny-by-default
  - PR-28241 denial reason codes + debug header
  - PR-28292 audit log authz decision fields
  - PR-28344 integration tests for critical permissions (existing partial; this ticket extends + adds CI guardrails)
- Incident learning:
  - Missing/bypassed permission check on streaming endpoint -> PR-28391 hotfix + regression test required.

Open questions
1) Do we want to require audit-log assertions for every critical action test, or keep it to representative sampling to avoid fragile coupling?
   - Proposal: enforce audit assertions for 3–5 key flows; rely on schema unit tests for the rest.
2) What’s the exact “deny reason code” contract for non-admin users?
   - We should assert stable high-level codes only (e.g., PERMISSION_DENIED, SCOPE_MISMATCH) and avoid codes that may change as evaluator evolves.

Rollout plan
- Week 1: land manifest + 6–8 core tests; run CI gate in warn-only mode.
- Week 2: expand to full critical list; flip CI gate to blocking; add dashboard for failure counts/flakes.

Definition of Done
- CI is blocking on:
  - failing integration tests in authz_critical_permissions
  - missing permission annotations for protected endpoints
  - missing manifest entries for newly introduced critical permissions
- Documented in repo (CONTRIBUTING / security testing section) how to add a new critical permission test.
comments: 2025-02-14 (Leila Farouk): Started drafting the manifest format + mapping for the initial critical list. Pulling from permission inventory endpoint audit + the bypass incident on streaming route. Need confirmation from Jordan on which denial reason codes are stable to assert in tests.

2025-02-18 (Jordan Lee): Reason codes: please only assert top-level codes in e2e (PERMISSION_DENIED, SCOPE_MISMATCH). Avoid asserting evaluator-internal codes; those may shift with caching + policy versioning changes. Also recommend running requests through gateway to catch missing route protection.

2025-02-20 (Amara Diallo): Gateway route table generator can emit a JSON artifact in CI. We can leverage that for guardrails (Option 2) if service annotation scrape gets messy. Prefer Option 1 long-term because it catches service-side gaps too.

2025-02-27 (Benji Okafor): Control plane endpoints now mostly annotated, but a couple of admin-only routes still missing (user deactivation + one routing policy update). I’ll file follow-ups; please make CI gate warn-only until these are fixed.

2025-03-06 (Kevin Osei): For audit log assertions, test should validate authz decision fields exist and are populated: actor, action, scope, decision, policy_version. Don’t assert the full SIEM payload shape in this suite (that belongs in exporter tests).

2025-03-14 (Leila Farouk): Implemented 7 integration tests (key rotation, create/revoke key, create role binding, delete role binding, edit routing policy, export audit logs deny, streaming generation deny). Tests currently ~9m in CI. Next: wire verify-permission-coverage script + run in warn-only mode for a week.
2025-03-22 (Connor O'Brien): Please coordinate enabling the blocking gate with the release branch cut. We should avoid flipping the switch the day we branch for Private backports.
